chapter: Apollo years, Eubie Blake and failing eyesight
title: Meeting Eubie Blake in Boston and confusion over Army bands
summary: Whaley met Eubie Blake in Boston in 1918, and they sort out Jim Europe's 369th, Mikell's and his own 807th band.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So tell me about some of these other guys. Where did you first run into a guy like Eubie Blake, I know he's been around. He's older than you.
Eubie I met in Boston. They came up there with a show and I was playing down in Leminster and they bought the show into Worchester and they got stranded. That was way back in 1918, I think.
Right after the war, because he was in that other band, wasn't he. Was Eubie in that band with -- what was his name, Jim Europe band.
Sissle was in there, wasn't he.
No, no, after he come out there.
I'm talking about in the Army. The 69th band.
I don't know, Jim Europe had that band.
Remember Gene Mikells*, his father was in that band.
Yeah, Mikells had a pioneer band, I think.
You were in the pioneer band.
Yeah, I was in 807 and I think Mikells had 808. He was from Baltimore, wasn't he.
Yeah, his son lives right up the street from -- but I thought he was in the -- he was a lieutenant in that 369th band.
He may have been. I didn't know because see I didn't meet any of them guys, when I was in the army, Jim Europe's was a big band. We were a small band, see, we were just developing.
